subject: Private deployment orientation — tenant validation & network checklist
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medicore.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff for private deployment — Medicore tenant

Hi Jonas / Neha,

Thanks for the connectivity info earlier — Medicore is ready to start the private deployment onboarding for the tenant tied to DEAL-9742. We want to target a soft go-live window in late May but first need a short run through of your pre-reqs and a validation checklist so our infra team can prepare ACLs, BGP peering and KMS access.

Attached is a filled copy of our internal pre-req form (Pre-reqs_Form.pdf). High-level items we care about:
- IP ranges you expect to use for egress and internal NAT
- TLS termination expectations (Redwood managed vs. customer)
- Where KMS/HSM integrations will land (we use AWS KMS/eHSM for key escrow)
- Expected maintenance windows / outage behavior

Can we schedule a 30-min technical orientation next week (Wed or Thu preferred)? Please advise who from Redwood will own the network checklist so we loop them in.

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Infrastructure, Medicore Health
Attachments: Pre-reqs_Form.pdf
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medicore.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-08T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff for private deployment — Medicore tenant

Thanks Liam — great to hear you're aiming for late May. I'm happy to own the orientation and the overall onboarding checklist, and Neha will lead the compliance/KMS items.

I've attached our working checklist (redwood-private-onboard-checklist_v1.xlsx) and pasted a condensed, actionable checklist below so your infra team can start aligning: 

1) Account & Access
- Provide tenant account owner (email) and IAM roles for provisioning (least privilege preferred).
- Service account for runtime agents with key rotation window.

2) Network Connectivity (what we need from Medicore)
- Public egress IP(s) or CIDR for outbound allowlist (for callbacks / health checks).
- VPC peering / PrivateLink details OR VPN endpoint + BGP ASN if you prefer routed connectivity.
- Firewall rules to allow inbound traffic from Redwood control plane (we'll provide IPs).
- DNS zone delegation plan for hostnames (optional if Redwood manages TLS).

3) Security & Keys
- KMS access: IAM principal(s) and grant scope for envelope encryption.
- Audit log destination and retention window (we commonly ship to customer S3 or SIEM).

4) Deployment & Test Steps
- Agent bootstrap method (S3 URL or private registry image) and service account secrets.
- Smoke tests: token-based generation, embeddings, and an upload/download cycle for cached artifacts.

5) Ops & Monitoring
- SNMP/Prometheus scrape endpoints or connector account for metrics ingestion.
- Pager/escalation contacts and severity mapping for SLO breaches.

Action items for Medicore: please confirm the outbound egress IPs/CIDR and your preference for TLS termination (Medicore or Redwood). Also share a calendar window for a 30-min kick-off next Wed (2028-04-11) morning if possible.

I'll loop in Ben for the low-level network port list and Laura for service account handoff.

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai
Attachments: redwood-private-onboard-checklist_v1.xlsx
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medicore.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-09T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff for private deployment — Medicore tenant (network details)

Following up with concrete network and port guidance so you can circulate to your network ops team. I've included a small template (network-templates.json) with example route maps. Link to a live copy: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcExampleOnboardFolder

Minimum network requirements (customer-facing):
- Outbound egress: allow 35.204.0.0/16 and 34.120.0.0/16 for control-plane callbacks (final list will be provided in the onboarding call).
- TLS: We support both sidecar TLS termination and customer-managed TLS at an edge LB. If Medicore terminates TLS, provide CN/SAN requirements and cert rotation cadence.
- Ports (customer -> Redwood):
  - 443 (HTTPS) for control-plane APIs and health probes
  - 5222 (optional) for internal agent heartbeat over mTLS if you use routed connectivity
  - 2379 (etcd) not used by Redwood directly — ensure isolation if present

Connectivity patterns supported (choose one):
- VPC Peering (preferred for AWS-to-AWS in-region) — exchange route tables and confirm no overlapping CIDR.
- PrivateLink / Interface Endpoint — if you prefer to avoid route table changes.
- Site-to-site VPN with BGP — provide ASN and IP allocator for BGP sessions.

KMS notes:
- If you provide KMS keys, create a dedicated key alias and grant Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey to the Redwood service principal.
- Rotate keys every 90 days recommended; we can support automatic key rotation hooks but need an IAM contact.

NTP & Time sync: confirm NTP servers for the environment; drift > 5s can cause token rejections.

Testing checklist (network team):
- Validate egress allowlist by curling a Redwood health endpoint we will provide.
- Confirm DNS resolution for the assigned hostnames and that cert chains validate from a public CA if you manage TLS.

Attachments: network-templates.json

Happy to present this on the kickoff. Laura, can you prepare the service account onboarding steps (IAM policy snippet + example least-privilege role)?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Network Integration Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medicore.com>

Cc: infra@medicore.com

Subject: Re: Kickoff for private deployment — Medicore tenant

Looking forward to the orientation and the checklist walk-through.

Best,
Liam
